lead.title: The AI Act deadline moved. The work didn't.
body: On 2 August the AI Act's transparency duties under Article 50 took effect on schedule, while the Digital Omnibus pushed stand-alone high-risk obligations out to December 2027 and AI embedded in regulated products to August 2028. The headline reads as relief. The detail reads as a deadline for the groundwork.

Research published this year found that more than half of organisations still hold no systematic inventory of the AI systems they operate, and that in a review of 106 enterprise systems, 40% could not be cleanly placed in a risk tier at all. Classification is the slow part, not remediation. For organisations running AI inside regulated delivery or public-sector programmes, the time bought is enough to build the inventory, classification and evidence trail once — and not enough to build it twice.

items.headline: AI Act transparency duties land; high-risk deadlines slip to 2027
items.summary: The Digital Omnibus defers stand-alone Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 and embedded high-risk systems to 2 August 2028. Article 50 disclosure duties began on 2 August 2026, with a grace period for watermarking existing systems until December.

items.headline: Sovereignty becomes a scored criterion in EU cloud procurement
items.summary: The Commission's Cloud Sovereignty Framework grades providers against 48 criteria in eight categories and assigns a Sovereignty Effectiveness Assurance Level. Public bodies are expected to apply it when buying cloud — turning jurisdictional exposure into a line item on the scorecard.

items.headline: Gartner: 40% of enterprise apps will ship task-specific AI agents this year
items.summary: Up from under 5% in 2025 — but Gartner also expects more than 40% of agentic AI projects to be cancelled by end-2027, citing unclear business value and weak governance rather than model capability. The differentiator is scoping, not tooling.
